workload.source: written here from the commit message of https://github.com/google/guava/commit/4802ac3c1be4ac806b8ca4477e5e875bb5f84e16 ("faster putInt, putChar, etc."): hashing a few primitives, a string and a byte array through a Hasher of Hashing.farmHashFingerprint64(), in process, warmed up until stable (eval/tasks/workloads/google-guava-4802ac3c1b/HasherWorkload.java)

oracle.source: FarmHashFingerprint64Test and HashingTest, the tests of the hash package AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction belongs to; targeted tests only

evidence.note: commit message: AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction.newHasher buffers in a ByteBuffer instead of a ByteArrayOutputStream

status_reason: built here, and the oracle ran on the task and reference trees (see runs); the workload was run too, but only in an earlier form (below). Built with the project's Maven wrapper and the JDK on the PATH (Eclipse Temurin 21); the jre flavour only. The oracle's surefire reports in the work tree, read after the run, show 47 tests run with no failure on each tree (FarmHashFingerprint64Test 6, HashingTest 40, collect.HashingTest 1); the recorded output tail does not carry them because the command runs with -q. The setup and oracle output tails say "Unable to locate a Java Runtime": that is printed by the macOS /usr/bin/java stub that the Maven wrapper probes (inference), and the build and the workload then ran with the JDK on the PATH (exit 0, jar built). The workload runs recorded here predate the warm-up rule now in the committed workload (a floor of 200 iterations, 1% tolerance, a cap of 600 that reports instead of failing); the iteration bodies are unchanged, but the program that ran is not the committed one, so workload.verified is false until it is run again on a quiet machine.
